findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator fails on datetime keys
findings.body: The new OptimizedCursorPaginator inherits from BasePaginator and overrides get_item_key to call math.floor/ceil on the attribute value. However, the endpoint uses this paginator with order_by="-datetime", so self.key is "datetime" and getattr(item, self.key) returns a datetime object. math.floor() cannot operate on a datetime, causing a TypeError on the first cursor building or result key computation. The original DateTimePaginator handles datetime fields, but this paginator does not. Any request with optimized_pagination=true will crash.

findings.title: Negative offset slicing on Django QuerySet raises an exception
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset < 0, the code executes results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop]) with a negative start_offset. Django QuerySets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError or ValueError ("Negative indexing is not supported"). The comment claims the ORM handles negative slicing automatically, which is false. This can be triggered by a client-provided cursor with a negative offset, causing a 500 error and potential denial of service for admins using the feature.

findings.title: Possible AttributeError when organization_context.member is None
findings.body: The expression organization_context.member.has_global_access assumes that member is not None. A superuser who is not a member of the organization may still pass permission checks (OrganizationAuditPermission often allows superusers regardless of membership), but in that case organization_context.member could be None. Accessing has_global_access on None will raise AttributeError and return a 500 instead of a proper response. Add a null check before dereferencing member.

findings.title: No tests for new optimized pagination path
findings.body: The PR adds a new paginator and a conditional code path (optimized_pagination=true) but includes no tests. The new paginator is broken for datetime keys and negative offsets, and the member dereference issue would not be caught without tests. At minimum, tests should cover the new endpoint query parameter, cursor generation, and handling of missing members.
